result.title: Pain Reassessment from Pulse Waveforms with Language Model Explanations
result.summary: Routine photoplethysmography (PPG) offers a continuous physiological signal for pain reassessment between self-reports. Whether prior recordings provide an individualized physiological reference beyond care-process timing remains unresolved. Across 52,082 report-linked assessments from 21,514 patients in MIMIC-III critical care and MC-MED emergency care, we evaluate a workflow that pairs longitudinal PPG representations with local evidence-linked language interpretation. Among 27 methods, source-selected full-history models achieved average precision of 0.824 from critical to emergency care and 0.822 in reverse. Removing historical pulse-run representations while retaining reassessment availability and elapsed time lowered critical-to-emergency four-hour within-patient concordance from 0.718 to 0.534. This comparison supports the contribution of prior pulse-run representations to within-patient ordering beyond timing cues. Across 2,905 test patients, a local Qwen model interpreting frozen predictions achieved a 94.7% patient-equal pass rate on automated evidence checks after at most one revision. Longitudinal pulse context and evidence-linked language interpretation support a patient-centred workflow for pain reassessment.

AI.brief_summary: 该文基于 MIMIC-III 与 MC-MED 的 5 万余条报告关联评估，将纵向 PPG 脉搏波表示与本地 LLM 生成的可溯源语言解释结合，用于两次自我报告之间的疼痛再评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「去掉历史脉搏段表示」的消融显示排序一致性显著下降，且用自动证据检查评估解释是否引用局部证据，这种贡献归因与证据核验流程可能为 LVR 中 latent 内容是否被使用及证据筛选的可信度评价提供参考。
